html:
The Hindu Code Bills were a set of laws passed by India's parliament in 1955 and 1956 that rewrote family law for Hindus and gave Hindu women rights to divorce and to inherit property.

B. R. Ambedkar, India's first law minister, drafted a single Hindu Code. Conservatives fought it hard, among them the president, Rajendra Prasad. In 1951 it stalled, and Ambedkar resigned in protest. After winning the 1952 election, Jawaharlal Nehru passed it in four parts:

  • The Hindu Marriage Act of 1955 banned polygamy and allowed divorce.
  • The Hindu Succession Act of 1956 let daughters and widows inherit.
  • Two acts of 1956 on guardianship and on adoption and maintenance.

The laws also cover Sikhs, Jains and Buddhists. They carried on the line of reform that began with the Widow Remarriage Act of 1856.

They were not complete. Daughters got equal shares in family property only after a change in 2005. And because Muslims and Christians kept their own personal laws, the bills fed a long debate over a uniform civil code.
sum: The Hindu Code Bills were a set of laws passed by India's parliament in 1955 and 1956 that rewrote family law for Hindus and gave Hindu women rights to divorce and to inherit property.
